answer: Bind each voting seat to a state falconry permit. To earn one, a person passes a wildlife-agency exam, serves a two-year apprenticeship under a licensed sponsor, and has their mews inspected before any bird is trapped. The permit names one keeper and one banded bird, so each seat traces to a real falcon hunting a real meadow. Exam, mews and gear cost about $5,000 per permit, so 400 sybil seats would cost an attacker roughly $2M plus 800 years of supervised apprenticeship. Seen through that prism, fake identities simply don't scale.
